iconicAnchor.label: Charles James couture as a sequenced study of silhouette and construction
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Haute couture presentation and fashion collection documentation
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Met presents iconic gowns through dramatic installation, detailed views, analytical animations, x-rays, pattern pieces, and grouped construction themes that together model a rigorous lookbook sequence.

sources.title: Charles James: Beyond Fashion
supports: Couture presentation benefits from full silhouettes, construction analysis, detail views, and a coherent grouping logic.
Dramatic display can remain informative when fabric, pattern, and garment architecture stay legible.

sources.title: Balenciaga: Shaping Fashion
supports: A collection can be taught through complete garments, work photographs, fabric details, and x-ray views of construction.
Repeated attention to silhouette and craftsmanship supports consistent editorial sequencing across multiple looks.

bundledReferenceRationale: The lead teaches a complete lookbook system through four aligned full-body looks and two fabric/construction details. Repetition and variation are clear, controlled, and legible at card scale. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/couture-lookbook/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
